title: Mutations
cheat_card: Mutations are permanent changes in DNA sequences, classified as germ-line (occur in gametes, inheritable) or somatic (occur in body cells, non-inheritable).

Spontaneous mutations result from replication errors (overall error rate of 1 in 1,000,000,000 nucleotides) or transposons; induced mutations are caused by environmental mutagens (e.g., UV radiation, tobacco smoke).
Point mutations alter a single nucleotide: silent mutations result in the same amino acid, missense mutations code for a different amino acid, and nonsense mutations code for a premature stop codon.
Frameshift mutations involve the insertion or deletion of 1 or 2 nucleotides, shifting the reading frame and rendering the resulting protein completely nonfunctional.
Cancer development involves accumulation of mutations: proto-oncogenes (stimulate cell cycle) mutate to hyperactive oncogenes, while tumor suppressor genes (inhibit cell division) are inactivated.
memory_anchor:
**Reading Frame Shift Example**:
- Normal message: `THE CAT ATE THE RAT` (triplets match)
- Deleted base ('C'): `THE ATA TET HER AT` (completely changes subsequent codons)
- Inserted base ('C'): `THE CCA TAT ETH ERA T` (completely shifts reading frame)

flashcards.q: Explain the difference between missense, nonsense, and silent point mutations in terms of their effect on the resulting protein's amino acid sequence.
flashcards.a: A silent mutation changes a single nucleotide but results in the same amino acid due to code degeneracy (no effect). A missense mutation changes a single nucleotide and codes for a different amino acid, potentially altering protein function. A nonsense mutation changes a codon into a premature stop codon, terminating translation early and producing a truncated, nonfunctional protein.

flashcards.q: Why do insertions or deletions of 1 or 2 nucleotides cause much more severe damage to proteins than insertions or deletions of 3 nucleotides?
flashcards.a: Insertions or deletions of 1 or 2 nucleotides shift the triplet reading frame of the entire mRNA sequence downstream of the mutation (frameshift), changing every subsequent amino acid. An insertion or deletion of 3 nucleotides adds or removes exactly one amino acid without disrupting the reading frame of the rest of the protein.

flashcards.q: How do mutations in proto-oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes cooperatively lead to the development of cancer?
flashcards.a: Proto-oncogenes normally stimulate cell division; when mutated into oncogenes, they become hyperactive, promoting uncontrolled cell division. Tumor suppressor genes normally inhibit cell division or repair DNA; when mutated, they lose function. Together, the cell cycle accelerator is stuck 'on' and the brakes are lost.

outline_blanks: A change in a single nucleotide is a [[point mutation]]. If the change creates a premature stop codon, it is a [[nonsense mutation]]. An insertion or deletion of 1 or 2 nucleotides causing a shift in the triplet reading frame is a [[frameshift mutation]], whereas cancer results from mutations in [[proto-oncogenes]] and [[tumor suppressor genes]].
